A security release with fixes from a review of how lazybw handles the vault,
the clipboard and Bitwarden's answers. Your configuration keeps working as it
is.

lazybw is now also on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/lazybw):
`cargo install --locked lazybw`.

## What's new

- Items that ask for the master password again hide their verification code
  until it is revealed, like the password.
- A lock that arrives while `$EDITOR` or another program has the terminal
  clears the decrypted vault and locks the CLI at once.
- A clipboard helper that hangs is killed with its process group, so it
  cannot write an old value later, and a lock drops copies still queued. A
  slow helper no longer freezes the interface.
- Answers from Bitwarden only reach the request that sent them: a save
  updates only the editor that sent it, and passwords generated at the same
  time each go to their own item.
- With a `bw` too old for the password report, vault health still runs its
  own checks.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SyscallBrain/lazybw/blob/v1.2.1/CHANGELOG.md)
has the full list.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `lazybw-1.2.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on x86_64 (static binary) |
| `lazybw-1.2.1-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on ARM64, including Termux on Android |
| `lazybw_1.2.1-1_amd64.deb`, `lazybw_1.2.1-1_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.2.1-1.x86_64.rpm`, `lazybw-1.2.1-1.aarch64.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.2.1-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`, `lazybw-1.2.1-1-aarch64.pkg.tar.zst` | Arch Linux, Arch Linux ARM |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums of all of the above |

On Arch Linux it is also in the AUR, as `lazybw-bin` (this release's binary)
and `lazybw` (built from source).

The container image with `bw` included is on the GitHub Container Registry:

```sh
docker run -it --rm -v lazybw:/home/lazybw ghcr.io/syscallbrain/lazybw:1.2.1
```

lazybw needs the official Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) 2025.9.0 or newer. The
[user guide](https://syscallbrain.github.io/lazybw/) covers installation and
everything else.
